stories.title: DeepSeek just open-sourced its inference engine
stories.blurb: DeepSeek drops DeepInfer on GitHub — a production-grade inference engine to go alongside their already formidable model lineup. Open-sourcing the full stack means you can now self-host DeepSeek end-to-end, no API middleman required. If you care about controlling your AI pipeline, this is a significant unlock.

stories.title: Ask HN: How to deal with shipping AI-written code you don't understand?
stories.blurb: The elephant in the room for every Claude Code user: what do you do when the AI writes a 200-line function and you're not sure you could defend it in a code review? 637 comments of hard-won practitioner wisdom here. Essential reading for anyone shipping AI-assisted code professionally.

stories.title: WhatsApp's help pages hid LLM instructions: dont recommend a regulator
stories.blurb: Researchers found hidden system-prompt instructions buried in WhatsApp's public help pages instructing its LLM-powered support bot never to recommend regulatory authorities to users with complaints. It's a textbook example of prompt injection surface area meeting corporate incentive misalignment — and a reminder that 'AI-powered support' can be quietly adversarial.

stories.title: It's still ok to enjoy programming
stories.blurb: In an era of AI coding assistants and 'just vibe-code it' takes, this post is a quiet, defiant argument that the craft of programming still has intrinsic value. 564 HN comments suggest this hit a nerve across the spectrum — from AI maximalists to old-school craftspeople. A good read before you open Claude Code today.

stories.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash
stories.blurb: MiniMax ships a new fast-inference model in the Flash tier, aimed squarely at latency-sensitive agentic applications. The competitive long-context window and aggressive pricing make it worth benchmarking against your current stack. Another week, another serious challenger in the inference race.

stories.title: How abliterated models can get you pwned
stories.blurb: ProjectDiscovery digs into the security risks of 'abliterated' (safety-stripped) LLMs — models that have had refusal mechanisms surgically removed. The attack surface is real: running one in a networked context can expose you to prompt-driven exploits that a safety-tuned model would block. If you self-host local models, read this.

stories.title: Agentic Monitoring
stories.blurb: As AI agents run longer and touch more systems, traditional observability tooling falls short. This post lays out a practical framework for monitoring agentic workflows — what to log, when to alert, and how to reason about non-deterministic execution paths. Directly actionable if you're building or running agents.

stories.title: Plex vulnerabilities being exploited in the wild to drop a cryptominer
stories.blurb: Active exploitation of Plex Media Server vulnerabilities is being used to silently deploy cryptominers on home and small-business servers. If you run Plex, patch now — or at minimum, ensure it's not exposed to the internet. A timely reminder that self-hosted media servers are a real attack surface.

stories.title: Nordwand Mono – A monospace font for coders and adventurers
stories.blurb: A new open-source monospace font built specifically for long coding sessions, with a Nordic/mountaineering aesthetic that pairs beautifully with dark themes. Free to use, carefully hinted, and the ligature support looks solid. Drop it into your editor and see if it sticks.

stories.title: France's supermarket fridges were vulnerable online for months
stories.blurb: Thousands of commercial refrigeration units across French supermarkets were left internet-accessible with default credentials for months, exposing both food-safety control systems and internal network footholds. A vivid IoT security horror story with real-world supply chain consequences.

stories.title: I built a drone with only one motor [video]
stories.blurb: Against all aerodynamic intuition, this engineer coaxed a drone into controlled flight using a single motor — achieving directional control through carefully tuned gyroscopic effects and passive blade geometry. Beautifully counterintuitive engineering that got 600 upvotes for good reason.

stories.title: OpenBSD 8.0
stories.blurb: OpenBSD 8.0 lands with updated GPU driver support pulled from Linux 6.18 (inteldrm, amdgpu), security hardening improvements, and the usual meticulous changelog. If you run OpenBSD on modern hardware, the improved GPU story is the headline upgrade here.

stories.title: An ad-free Android TV
stories.blurb: A practical guide to reclaiming your Android TV from the ad-stuffed, data-harvesting default experience — covering sideloading, ADB tweaks, custom launchers, and Pi-hole integration. Actionable weekend project for anyone tired of being marketed at on their own television.

stories.title: Putting Linux on my RTX Spark laptop because I don't have a Microsoft account
stories.blurb: A firsthand account of being forced onto Linux by Windows 11's mandatory Microsoft account requirement — and finding the experience surprisingly smooth on new NVIDIA hardware. The privacy frustration is relatable; the outcome is a good field report on the current state of Linux laptop support.

stories.title: DeepSeek banned from U.S. federal civilian agencies under new DHS order
stories.blurb: DHS has formally prohibited DeepSeek from all federal civilian agency IT systems, citing national security concerns. The order has ripple effects for any developer building on DeepSeek for government clients — and signals that the AI model geopolitics are hardening fast.

stories.title: MicroG: Free-libre re-implementation of Google's proprietary Android user space
stories.blurb: MicroG resurfaces on HN as the go-to solution for running Android apps without the Google Play Services surveillance layer. If you're building de-Googled Android setups or recommending privacy-respecting mobile configs to users, this wiki is the canonical starting point.

stories.title: RuneScape Bench: MMOs for Agents [video]
stories.blurb: Researchers use RuneScape as a benchmark environment for AI agents — it turns out MMOs are surprisingly good proxies for real-world long-horizon task completion. The evaluation methodology here is clever and has implications beyond games for anyone designing agentic evals.

stories.title: Restoration of Retinal Regenerative Potential (2025)
stories.blurb: A Nature paper showing that mammalian retinal cells retain regenerative potential that can be chemically reactivated — a meaningful step toward treatments for degenerative eye disease. The biology here is genuinely surprising; photoreceptor regeneration was long thought impossible in mammals.

stories.title: Google cloud outage takes down banks
stories.blurb: A Google Cloud outage cascaded through HSBC, Revolut, Lloyds, Bank of Scotland, and Equifax simultaneously — a vivid reminder of how much critical financial infrastructure now runs on a handful of hyperscalers. If your own services depend on GCP, this is worth a post-mortem read.

stories.title: One Hash Bloom Filters
stories.blurb: A well-written explainer on a variant of Bloom filters that uses only a single hash function — achieving surprisingly competitive false-positive rates with simpler implementation and better cache behavior. Pure CS sweetness with practical implications for high-throughput lookup systems.
